exposure: peripheral immune markers (neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, platelets)
cohort: The study involved 19,028 women with singleton pregnancies between January 2020 and December 2023, with peripheral immune markers measured during gestational weeks 11-28.
finding: Higher peripheral neutrophil, lymphocyte, and platelet levels were significantly associated with an increased risk of preeclampsia, especially in older pregnant women, although Mendelian randomization analysis did not support a causal link.
